ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Judy Garland

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Garland is a 33-year-old singer and actor with a barbiturate use disorder on a phenobarbital taper, a mild stimulant use disorder in early remission, chronic insomnia, and depression with anxiety on sertraline, who comes for her yearly preventive visit four weeks after her ten-week review and six months after the birth of her third child. She has followed the written taper schedule: the step two weeks ago went smoothly, and today is her next planned step, to 40.5 mg a day. She has taken no secobarbital, dextroamphetamine, or any other sedative or stimulant. She sleeps about six hours on most nights with her CBT-I routine and a fixed wake time, even after late rehearsals. Her mood and worry are better, and her PHQ-9 today is 7. She eats three meals on most days. She is due for her second contraceptive injection. She still smokes about ten cigarettes a day. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 17 minutes, with her consent. She named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. She said that what matters most to her is her children, her work, and being treated as a person rather than a problem. She asked that, if she were ever too ill to speak for herself, her treatment for the pills be continued without blame. She chose not to record specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
